question: Should consecutive malformed pullAudio payloads count toward the existing five-error cutoff and terminate the Google Meet audio bridge?
rationale: Both rejecting malformed audio and continuing valid traffic are clearly correct, but whether repeated protocol-invalid payloads should end an active meeting bridge is an availability policy choice that code and CI cannot settle.

options.title: Reuse the existing cutoff
options.body: Treat each malformed payload as an input failure and close after five consecutive failures, matching other repeated node-input errors.

options.title: Reject without consuming cutoff
options.body: Drop malformed payloads and warn without advancing the shutdown counter, preserving bridge availability at the cost of potentially retrying a persistently broken node indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Reuse the existing cutoff
recommendation.body: Treat each malformed payload as an input failure and close after five consecutive failures, matching other repeated node-input errors.
